subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in core `models status --probe --all` mode, and what exact contract should it use for cost, rate limits, JSON fields, agent scoping, and fallback-chain overlap?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a live probe mode changes user-visible CLI behavior and provider call costs, and related issues already propose fallback-chain and migration-test diagnostics.

options.title: Approve Bounded Core Probe
options.body: Add `--probe --all` to the existing status command with default behavior unchanged, explicit docs, typed JSON output, bounded concurrency/timeouts, and live proof.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback Diagnostics
options.body: Keep this issue open but make it part of a broader fallback-chain health command so OpenClaw does not ship overlapping probe modes.

options.title: Decline Core Mode
options.body: Leave ongoing multi-model monitoring to external tools or plugins and keep core focused on the existing provider/profile auth probe.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Core Probe
recommendation.body: Add `--probe --all` to the existing status command with default behavior unchanged, explicit docs, typed JSON output, bounded concurrency/timeouts, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the current live model status probe surface and is the strongest routing candidate for the product contract decision.
